title: Lower support bound for double derived Hom with bounded injective targets
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $E,L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $q,u,v\in\mathbf Z$. Suppose $H^r(E)=0$ for $r<q$. Let $J,I$ be bounded cochain complexes of injective $R$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], equipped with isomorphisms $J\cong L$ and $I\cong M$ in $D(R)$, such that $J^r=0$ for $r>u$ and $I^r=0$ for $r<v$. Use derived internal Hom on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every complex $B$ representing $E$ with $B^r=0$ for $r<q$, put $C=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(B,J)$ and $D=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(C,I)$. There are isomorphisms in $D(R)$
$$C\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L),\qquad D\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L),M).$$
These actual model complexes satisfy $C^s=0$ for $s>u-q$ and $D^t=0$ for $t<q+v-u$. In particular $H^t(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L),M))=0$ for $t<q+v-u$. The same integers $u,v$ apply to every $E$ and $q$ satisfying the given hypotheses.

proof.text: The cohomological hypothesis on $E$ says that $E\in D(R)^{\ge q}$. By the cohomology/representative equivalence in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], there exists a representing complex $B$ with $B^p=0$ for $p<q$. Fix any such representative, as the statement permits; the subsequent argument works for each of them.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle, lower truncation; the representative equivalence is also Mathlib DerivedCategory.isGE_iff.

proof.text: Since $J$ is bounded, some integer $a$ satisfies $J^p=0$ for $p<a$; $I$ is already zero below $v$. Both have injective terms by hypothesis. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective] in the abelian category of $R$-modules, first with lower bound $a$ and then with lower bound $v$. Thus both $J$ and $I$ are K-injective. No injectivity hypothesis on $B$ or on $C$ is needed.

On the one-object site with trivial topology and coefficient ring $R$, the derived internal Hom construction [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] may use any K-injective representative for its second argument. Its independence from the resolution and from the first representative is justified by [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined]. Apply this with source $B$ and target $J$ to obtain $QC\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L)$, where $Q$ is localization. Apply it again with source $C$ and target $I$ to obtain $QD\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(QC,M)$. Finally apply the contravariant first-variable functor $R\operatorname{Hom}_R(-,M)$ to the first isomorphism and compose its inverse with the second, giving $QD\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_R(R\operatorname{Hom}_R(E,L),M)$. These are isomorphisms in $D(R)$, with no boundedness assumption on $C$.

source.place: Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom, choice of representatives and bifunctor; Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined.

proof.text: By [def-pur-hom-complex], $C^s=\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_R(B^p,J^{p+s})$. Suppose $s>u-q$. For every $p<q$ the source $B^p$ is zero. For every $p\ge q$ one has $p+s\ge q+s>u$, so $J^{p+s}=0$. Every factor is therefore the zero module, and their product is zero (its only family is the family of zero maps). Consequently $C^s=0$ for $s>u-q$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product formula; expanded support calculation for more-algebra.tex Tag 0A69, final sentence of proof.

proof.text: Again [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $D^t=\prod_{s\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_R(C^s,I^{s+t})$. Let $t<q+v-u$. If $s>u-q$, the source is zero by Step 4. If $s\le u-q$, then $s+t\le u-q+t<v$, so the target is zero by the hypothesis on $I$. Thus all factors, and hence the product, are zero. This proves the claimed actual-complex support bound $D^t=0$ below $q+v-u$.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, section-hom-complexes, product formula; expanded support calculation for more-algebra.tex Tag 0A69, final sentence of proof.

proof.text: For $t<q+v-u$, Step 5 gives $D^t=0$, so $\ker(d_D^t)=0$ and $H^t(D)=\ker(d_D^t)/\operatorname{im}(d_D^{t-1})=0$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology factors through $Q$ and is functorial on $D(R)$. Applying it to the derived isomorphism of Step 3 proves the asserted vanishing of double derived Hom. The computations used only $J^{>u}=0$, $I^{<v}=0$ and $B^{<q}=0$; thus the same fixed $u,v$ work for every eligible $E,q$ and every chosen $B$, including zero complexes.
